name_reason: Compliant data_fd2_ game-global name. Domain descriptor chapter_event_handler_33 ties it to its sole consumer (per-event dispatch table @ 0x51B91, dispatch idx 0x33 -- a real domain ID, not an address residue; the address is 0x52748). drop_entry_inline correctly conveys the data type/purpose: an inline 3-byte battle-drop entry. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Inline 3-byte battle-drop entry constant consumed by fd2_chapter_event_handler_33__unref_drop: grants one ITEM (item id 101 = Teleport Staff) to the stepping char, then shows dialog page 3.
logic_summary: 3-byte drop entry { type=0x00 (ITEM), value=0x0065 (LE ushort) }. Handler 0x33 copies these 3 bytes (MOVSW + MOVSB at 0x352AB/0x352B0) to a stack local and calls fd2_process_battle_drop_entries(stepping_char_id, 1, &local). In the type-0 branch the entry value is the item id (0x65 = 101 = Teleport Staff / 傳送法杖), added to the recipient's inventory with the pickup dialog, then the handler shows chapter dialog page 3. The handler slot is unreferenced by any chapter FDFIELD turn-event/tile-step hook (cut content).
element_semantics: Battle-drop entry: byte[0] = entry type (0=ITEM, 1=GOLD, 2=battle-event, 3=scripted-dialog) = 0x00 ITEM here; byte[1..2] = little-endian ushort value = 0x0065. For type 0 the value is an item id -> 0x65 (101) = 傳送法杖 (Teleport Staff).
notes: is_const=true: Ghidra xrefs to 0x52748 are only READ (0x352B0 MOVSW) and DATA (0x352AB MOV ESI,0x52748 immediate) from the single consumer; zero game-side writer, so genuinely read-only -- src already declares it 'static const'. Name verdict keep, no rename queued for Stage 2. comment_verdict=keep: existing chevt2.c block comment (lines 154-189) already precisely documents the 3-byte entry (type=0 ITEM, value=0x0065 -> item id 101 = Teleport Staff, verified against fd2-knowledge) plus the borrowed-tail size optimisation; concise and final, no edit needed, so src/field/chevt2.c is unmodified. ghidra_plate_action=created: the data PLATE_COMMENT was empty while the documentation sat (non-canonically) in PRE_COMMENT; migrated a refined version (now including the verified item id) into PLATE_COMMENT and cleared PRE_COMMENT per project data-plate convention.
